items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: This is the trio. This is Stuff Smith’s trio, the group that I came to New York with.

ctx.x: Who was coming in and around? What bands were coming in that you followed in Chicago?

During that period of time, it wasn’t that much travel – about bands traveling, coming and going. You had places where these musicians worked. They stayed in that one club for over a year, sometimes as long as two years. So you had Joe Glaser’s club, Sunset Club, where the bands like Fletcher Henderson were. They worked there for – and Earl Hines – they worked there for long periods of time, and they were on the air broadcasting every night. Benny Goodman worked at the Congress Hotel for over a year, working…
Which group is this? This is the . . .

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: So I met Stuff and there was Raymond Walters was the piano player that had been chosen to work with Stuff. It was just a trio — violin, piano and bass. So we had this engagement downtown... my first experience of really making money was really with George Shearing because up to that point, even with

ctx.x: Don’t quit your day gig, right?

Yeah, that’s the thing. Yeah that’s something else. So we spent a lot of time, you know, learning about the inside of the business. For example at that time the musicians’ union was very strong so you had to, in each city you went to play you had to report to the union and so I learned all about that part of the business. And by accident, here again I use the word accident, I was working in the post office and the president of the musicians’ union, the Local 208 which was the black local in Chicago at the time,…
Wrong city to come to, right?
